subject: Residency cutover: KMS handoff and validation windows

Subject: Redwood private deployment - KMS handoff and acceptance windows

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment options yesterday. Before we lock dates with procurement, Security needs a clear plan for the KMS handoff and the validation window for the EU->APAC warm standby cutover. Two items we need answered: 1) Are customer-managed keys (BYOK) supported in the private VPC topology, and 2) what is the measurable acceptance criteria for a successful cutover (visibility/metrics/hooks we can validate)?

Can you share the network diagram and the key-control policy draft so we can run this past our internal KMS team?

Best,

Date: 2028-08-13T11:20:00Z
From: logan_wright@redwood.ai
To: Erik Svensson <erik.svensson@nordbank.se>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Redwood private deployment - KMS handoff and acceptance windows

Erik — short answers up front: yes, BYOK is supported for private VPC and we provide a concrete validation checklist for cutovers. Links to artifacts below.

High-level BYOK flow:
- Customer provisions CMK in their KMS (Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS / CloudHSM) and creates a service key alias we reference for model-serving.
- Customer grants Redwood a narrowly scoped role (Encrypt/Decrypt/Wrap/Unwrap) limited by key alias and time window. RW never stores plaintext key material; we perform envelope encryption and ephemeral wrapping.

Control/data separation notes:
- Control plane (deploy orchestration, rollouts) options: Redwood-managed in your VPC peering OR customer-managed control plane using our control-plane appliance.
- Data plane (model inference, cache, and KV) is pinned to the region-specific cluster (EU or APAC) and does not egress outside designated CIDRs.

Proposed acceptance signals (we'll formalize):
1) Key handshake: test object encrypted by RW using your CMK and successfully decrypted by your KMS; KMS audit log entry present with request-id.
2) Trace residency: 10 sampled inference requests show spans with region tag and only allowed egress IPs.
3) KV residency: KV cache warm-up verification shows no replication outside target region during window.
4) SLO check: p95 latency not exceeding agreed SLO for 95% of requests during the 4-hour window.
5) Rollback trigger: if any of the above fail, automatic traffic flip-back within 15 minutes.

Artifacts: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/residency/DB-2028-1337/diag-v2 (network-diagram-v2.pdf)
https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/residency/DB-2028-1337/kms-key-policy (kms-key-policy.docx)
https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/residency/DB-2028-1337/checklist (residency-acceptance-checklist.xlsx)

I'll draft a formal 4-hour validation playbook and a 30-minute cutover dry-run checklist by tomorrow morning. Marissa — can you confirm procurement lead times? Soojin — can you draft the residency verification script?

— Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: network-diagram-v2.pdf (link), kms-key-policy.docx (link)

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the clarity. A couple of region-specific questions from our side: 1) During the warm standby cutover, does the APAC cluster accept connections only from Japan/APAC egress ranges or do you open inter-region peering temporarily? 2) How do you validate KMS replication lag if the customer KMS is multi-region (we need evidence for our compliance team)?

Also, please include UTC and JST time examples in the validation playbook.

Regards,
Aiko Tanaka
Head of Cloud Engineering, Kumo Bank (APAC)

Attachments: none

Date: 2028-08-14T10:30:00Z
From: logan_wright@redwood.ai
To: Aiko Tanaka <aiko.tanaka@kumo-bank.jp>, Erik Svensson <erik.svensson@nordbank.se>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Residency cutover: KMS handoff and validation windows

Aiko — good questions. Short answers: we avoid temporary broad peering; warm standby uses controlled failover via smart routing and restricted peering only between designated cluster egress ranges. Details:

- Egress controls: APAC cluster will only accept inbound from listed customer NAT egress CIDRs and Redwood's managed egress set for the region. We do not open global peering for cutover.
- KMS replication evidence: during the handshake test we generate a KMS request-id and timestamp; customer KMS audit logs will show replication target timestamps. If your KMS exposes replication-status APIs (e.g., CloudHSM/Custom HSM), we include a snapshot in the acceptance evidence.

Validation playbook items (examples with UTC / JST):
- 09:00 UTC (18:00 JST): Start 30-min dry-run — encrypt/decrypt handshake and KV residency sample (10 traces).
- 09:30 UTC (18:30 JST): Begin 4-hour validation window — run 1,000 synthetic inferences at steady QPS; collect p95 latency and span traces every 15 minutes.
- Rollback at 10:15 UTC if any critical KMS error observed.

I'll attach a JST/UTC schedule table in the playbook. Soojin — will you add the trace export instructions and the sample query scripts?

— Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
